_note: Axis-A color conformance under a PERCEPTUAL color-loss metric: the analyzer decodes the OUTPUT by its own embedded tag and the SOURCE forced to its matrix/range (so the reference never rests on what ffmpeg would infer, which matters for the untagged charts), then asks 'does the export SHOW the same colors as the source?'. ALL FOUR encodings are FAITHFUL (worst_app_max <= faithfulMax). All four decode the ORIGINAL (DirectExport: a full-range yuvj420p source routes like yuv420p). A proxy of such a source is made self-describing by the recipe (source_color_args + write_colr, proxy v7/quick-q4) and its decode also takes the source's resolved colour -- mediabunny reads only the mp4 colr atom (never the SPS VUI) and the Chromium decoder follows the config over the VUI, so a colr-less proxy decode used to fall back to bt709/limited and misread full-range (pc-as-tv clip+stretch) and 601 (601-as-709) proxies. The decoder's frame then converts through VideoClipSprite's colorSpace-honoring 2D drawImage (Pixi's copyExternalImageToTexture ignores VideoFrame.colorSpace). The WebCodecs HD encoder ignores the input frame colorSpace and writes a resolution default, so every HD output is bt709/limited-tagged: 601 sources are faithfully NORMALIZED to 709 and full-range sources faithfully CONVERTED to limited, costing only codec round-trip. ADR 0014.
